## Data source

We use life table data from Hernández-Pacheco et al (2013) (Table A1) to re-create reproductive values for rhesus macaques shown in Hasegawa & Kutsukake (2019) (Figure 1).

```{r}
library(tidyverse)

p <- readxl::read_excel("Hernández-Pacheco_et_al_2013_A1.xlsx")

p$age <- p$`χ age`
p$mx <- p$Fx   #age-specific fertility
p$lx <- p$lχ   #probability of surviving from birth to age x
p$px <- p$`Pχ` #age-specific survival rate

p <- p |> select(age, mx, lx, px, Nχ) |> filter(is.na(age)==F)
p <- as.data.frame(p)

head(p)
```

## Create Leslie matrix

This is based on code provided by: 
https://shinyibv02.uio.no/content/0b6ba04a-44a1-4a99-baaf-9a1caff48698/s03-MatrixModels.html

```{r}
Create.Amat <- function(Svec, Fvec) {
	k <- length(Svec)
	MatA<- matrix(0,k,k)
	MatA[1,] <- Fvec 
	for(i in 1:(k-1)){
		MatA[i+1,i] <- Svec[i]
	}
	#Individuals can accumulate if Svec[k]>0:
	MatA[k,k] <- Svec[k] 
	MatA
}

# Leslie matrix
A <- Create.Amat(p$px, p$mx)
(A)
```

## Generate reproductive values based on projection matrix

Also based on code provided by: 
https://shinyibv02.uio.no/content/0b6ba04a-44a1-4a99-baaf-9a1caff48698/s03-MatrixModels.html

```{r}
# function where the input is the Leslie matrix (projection matrix)
## three outputs produced:
### [1] lambda: dominant eigenvalue of A (projection matrix)
### [2] u: right eigenvector
### [3] v: left eigenvector
uvlambda <- function(MatA){
	ev <- eigen(MatA)
	tev <- eigen(t(MatA))
	lmax <- which.max(Re(ev$values))
	U <- ev$vectors
	V <- tev$vectors
	u <- as.matrix(abs(Re(U[, lmax]))/sum(abs(Re(U[, lmax]))))
	u <- u/(sum(u)) #scale u
	v <- as.matrix(abs(Re(V[, lmax])))
	v <- v/sum(u*v ) #scale v
	v <- t(ifelse(u*v <= 0, 0, v))
	return(list("lambda"=max(Re(ev$values)),"u"=u,"v"=v))
}

l <- uvlambda(A)
(l)
```

```{r}
u.rhe <- l$u
v.rhe <- l$v

# data frame
asym <- data.frame("AgeClass"=0:30, "u"=u.rhe, "v"=t(v.rhe))

head(asym)
```


```{r}
#Long format for plotting:
asym.long <- asym |> 
  pivot_longer(c(u,v), names_to = "Vector", values_to = "Value")

#Ensure order of factor levels (for plotting)
asym.long$AgeClass <- factor(asym.long$AgeClass, levels=0:30)

ggplot(asym.long) + 
  geom_col(aes(x=AgeClass, y=Value, fill=AgeClass ), lwd=1.2)+
  theme_bw() +
  facet_wrap(vars(Vector), ncol=2, scales="free")+
  labs( x="Age class", y="Value")+ #Axis labels
  theme(legend.position = "None" ) #remove legend
```

panel 'u' above is the stable age structure, while panel 'v' are the reproductive values


## Check values against Hasegawa & Kutsukake (2019) (Figure 1)

```{r}
# plot
plot(x=asym$AgeClass, y=asym$v, type="l")

# re-scale values so that value at age 0 is 1
val <- asym$v[1]  #reproductive value, at age 0
x <- 1/val

# plot, re-scaled
plot(x=asym$AgeClass, y=asym$v * x, type="l")

# re-scale in dataframe
asym$Vx <- asym$v * x
asym$age <- as.integer(asym$AgeClass)
```


```{r}
repro_vals <- asym |> select(age, Vx)
summary(repro_vals)

write.csv(repro_vals, "data_rhe_repro_vals.csv", row.names=F)
```


# weighted, splines for non-linear effects

```{r}
library(brms)

weights <- p |> select(age, Nχ)
asym <- asym |> left_join(weights)

mod <- brm(Vx | weights(Nχ) ~ 1 + s(age), 
						data = asym, cores = 4, chains = 4, seed = 1977)

pp_check(mod)
```



```{r}
ages <- seq(0,32,0.1)
newdata <- data.frame(age = ages)

t <- predict(mod, newdata=newdata)
t <- data.frame(t)

t$age <- ages
t$Estimate[t$Estimate < 0] <- 0
t$Estimate[t$age > 25] <- 0

t <- t |> dplyr::select(age, Estimate) |> rename(Vx = Estimate)

summary(t)
```

```{r}
Vx_max <- max(t$Vx)
t |> filter(Vx == Vx_max)
```

```{r}
t |> filter(Vx == 0) |> head()
```


```{r}
ggplot(t, aes(x=age, y=Vx)) + 
	theme_classic(base_size = 24) + 
	geom_point(alpha = .75) + 
	geom_line(color = 'red', linewidth = .25) + 
	geom_point(data=asym, aes(x=age,y=Vx,size=`Nχ`), color='red') + 
	geom_vline(xintercept = 4.8,  linetype = 3) + #max
	geom_vline(xintercept = 23.6, linetype = 3) + #min
	annotate("text", x= 4.8 + 1.5, y=1, label = "4.8") + 
  annotate("text", x=24.1 + 1.5, y=1, label = "23.6") + 
	labs(y=expression(paste("reproductive value ( ", italic(V)[X], " )"))) + 
	theme(legend.position = 'none')

ggsave('subFig_repro_values_rhe.pdf', device = 'pdf', width=20, height=20, 
			 units='cm', colormodel = 'rgb', dpi = 300)
```

```{r}
write.csv(t, "data_repro_values_rhe.csv", row.names=F)
```
